tables.how: Every “CampaignContributionMade” entry in the lobbyist activity file is joined to the “ContactOfPublicOfficial” entries of the same lobbyist with the same official (surname and first name), and kept when a contact falls within 365 days either side: 1,085 entries since 2010, 119 of them dated 2018 or later ($94,975). The kind of committee is read from its name: City office (96 since the ban, $33,775), a seat on the local party committee (15, $18,500), a ballot-measure or independent committee (3, $25,000), State or regional office (5, $17,700). Rows since the ban come first.
tables.limits: No row is a finding that a contribution was unlawful. The 2018 rule applies only if the lobbyist was registered to lobby that official’s agency then or in the prior 90 days, and this file does not give the agencies; the match here uses reported contacts within twelve months. Lobbyists must also report contributions by their employers and sometimes their clients, so an entry that names someone else as the source can be the disclosure of that person’s own gift, not money the lobbyist collected. Party-committee, ballot-measure and State campaigns are outside the City’s limit and the lobbyist ban. The official is matched by name as the lobbyist typed it.
